description: SDLC-support products that help plan, implement, review, test, secure, modernize, or maintain software. General-purpose agent application platforms, frameworks, eval tools, and guardrails live in agents.json.

categories.description: Agents that can take tickets, prompts, issues, or tasks and independently modify repositories, run tests, and produce pull requests or deployable application changes.
Interactive coding agents embedded in IDEs, terminals, editors, or local developer environments.
Enterprise developer-platform agents that combine coding, repository intelligence, cloud context, DevSecOps workflows, governance, modernization, and organizational controls.
Agents focused on pull request review, bug finding, standards enforcement, test coverage, CI feedback, and code quality governance.

options.name: OpenAI Codex Agent
options.notes: Coding agent for CLI, desktop, IDE, and cloud tasks with skills, plugins, MCP, and repository tools. CLI 0.153.4 (September 4) makes GPT-6 Astra the default, following plugin marketplace CLI support in 0.153.0; GPT-5.4 access through ChatGPT-authenticated Codex ended August 31, while API-key use remains available.

options.name: Claude Code
options.notes: Coding agent spanning CLI, IDE, desktop, web, remote sessions, and team workflows, with subagents, skills, plugins, and MCP. September releases add skill-use diagnostics, organization-policy diagnostics, configurable command-output limits, and file-based subagent prompts; version 2.1.263 was released September 6.

options.name: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent
options.notes: Background coding agent for issues, pull requests, and repository tasks across GitHub and supported developer tools. September updates add Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash access, content exclusions in CLI/app workflows, and VS Code Agent Merge in public preview for review feedback, failing CI, and merge conflicts.

options.name: Devin
options.notes: Autonomous software engineering agent for implementation, remediation, review, and maintenance tasks, with cloud, desktop, and customer-hosted Outpost execution. August updates add nested SubDevins and enterprise MCP controls; September 2 adds cleanup scans, /scan, and recurring scans through Automations.

options.name: Factory Droids
options.notes: Software development agents for CLI, desktop, web, IDE, CI/CD, and enterprise workflows. Late-August releases add editable queued messages, Droid doctor diagnostics, and stronger MCP recovery; CLI 0.209.0/Desktop 0.166.0 (September 1) add session archiving and GPT-5.6 Sol as the default model for unconfigured sessions.

options.name: Replit Agent
options.notes: App-building agent that writes code, configures infrastructure, tests, and deploys projects from Replit workspaces. Project Analytics (September 4) adds paid custom events and conversion funnels, which Agent can help instrument and analyze.

options.name: Cursor Background Agents
options.notes: Asynchronous coding agents with cloud environments, branch workflows, scheduled or event-triggered subscriptions, steering, and subagents that can use separate virtual machines. Since September 2, agents can also execute on personal or team-managed machines, with worker pools, autoscaling, and Linux/macOS computer use.

options.name: Google Antigravity 2.0
options.notes: Development environment with parallel agents, custom agents, scheduling, CLI/SDK access, and managed cloud execution. August releases add embedded terminals, Git controls, and inline interactive HTML artifacts; September 2 adds /boost multi-agent reasoning, followed by Gemini 3.8 Flash access through enterprise credentials on September 3.

options.name: Mistral Vibe
options.notes: Work and coding agent with local and remote sessions, long-running tasks, skills, MCP, and file and terminal tools. Agentic Search arrived in Vibe Libraries on August 20, letting agents navigate and verify information across complex documents.

options.name: Cursor
options.notes: Agentic IDE and development workspace for coding, debugging, repository chat, and multi-agent work. Origin code hosting entered early beta for paid users August 17; August 27 added starting projects from scratch with live previews and Vercel publishing, and September 2 added agent execution on customer-managed machines.

options.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
options.notes: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (renamed June 2, 2026 after Cognition's acquisition); Devin Local has replaced Cascade as the default local agent, with Cascade-specific configuration being phased out. Devin Desktop v3.7.x (Aug 2026) adds shareable Devin Local conversations, editor-file context awareness, persistent 'Always Allow' permissions, and MCP auth fixes.

options.name: Cline
options.notes: Open-source coding agent that runs in the editor, reads and writes files, executes terminal commands with user approval, uses browser/tools, supports MCP, and works with user-provided model keys.

options.name: Aider
options.notes: Terminal-first AI pair programmer with whole-repo maps, Git-native diffs and commits, support for many languages, and broad model-provider compatibility.

options.name: Continue
options.notes: Local-first IDE coding agent and assistant with model-agnostic context streaming, custom tools, and repo-aware development workflows.

options.name: Sourcegraph Cody
options.notes: AI coding assistant backed by Sourcegraph code search and codebase context. Helps understand, write, debug, and maintain code across local and remote repositories.

options.name: JetBrains Junie
options.notes: Coding agent for JetBrains IDEs and CLI that plans, edits, tests, and debugs projects. Junie Local launched August 24 with a tuned Qwen3.6-27B model running entirely on an M5 Mac with at least 64 GB of RAM, without subscription or usage credits.

options.name: Grok Build
options.notes: Local-first coding agent with planning and review modes, repository edits, shell execution, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, and subagents. xAI open-sourced Grok Build in July 2026.

options.name: Qwen Code
options.notes: Open-source coding agent for terminal, editor, and Web Shell with tools, memory, plugins, MCP, subagents, and scheduling. Stable v0.23.0 (September 3) adds scoped memory tasks, fresh sessions for scheduled runs, workflow execution controls, and named-session messaging.

options.name: Kimi Code
options.notes: Coding agent with terminal, web, and IDE workflows, plugins, tools, and subagents. v0.40 (September 2) makes the subagent model pool generally available and adds a web plugin panel; v0.41 (September 4) adds experimental Tower collaboration in the web interface, following experimental remote control in August.

options.name: GitHub Copilot
options.notes: Developer-platform assistant for completion, chat, coding-agent delegation, repository context, and code review across GitHub and IDEs. September updates include the JetBrains agent harness at general availability and optional Copilot pull-request approvals in public preview, disabled by default until an administrator enables them.

options.name: Amazon Q Developer
options.notes: AWS developer assistant for coding, review, upgrades, cloud guidance, and operations. Its IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on April 30, 2027; AWS directs developer-workflow users to Kiro, while Q in the AWS Console and chat apps continues.

options.name: Kiro
options.notes: AWS development environment for specifications, steering, hooks, powers, plugins, and governed agent workflows. Kiro Web became generally available September 1, with cloud configuration sync into local IDE and CLI sessions and a CLI dashboard for local and cloud sessions.

options.name: Gemini Code Assist Agent Mode
options.notes: Agent mode for Gemini Code Assist that uses IDE context, built-in tools, terminal actions, and MCP servers to solve multi-step software tasks, generate code from issues or design docs, and run controlled tool actions.

options.name: GitLab Duo with Amazon Q
options.notes: Agentic DevSecOps integration that embeds Amazon Q software development agents into GitLab workflows for feature development, quality, security, pipeline troubleshooting, and Java modernization.

options.name: CodeRabbit
options.notes: AI code review and 'Agentic Change Management' platform: context-aware PR review, IDE/CLI review, planning from issues, Slack workflows, plus Triage (routing changes by value/risk), Change Stack (semantic explanation of large agent-generated diffs), and CodeRabbit Security (reachability-aware vulnerability detection and fixes in PRs), launched with a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation (Aug 12-13, 2026).

options.name: Qodo
options.notes: AI code review and governance platform with multi-agent review, repository context, Rule Miner (learns rules from past reviews), Review Effort Modes with adaptive depth routing, standards governance, bug finding, and shift-left review in IDE, CLI, and Kiro workflows.

options.name: Lovable
options.notes: App-creation agent with hosting, integrations, security scanning, and enterprise controls. September updates add domain setup through chat with purchase confirmation, Slack availability across all plans, workspace adoption analytics, and Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash for video features in generated apps.

options.name: Augment Code (Cosmos / Auggie)
options.notes: Coding platform combining Auggie CLI and IDE integrations with the Cosmos cloud workspace, repository context, MCP integrations, and remote agents. Auggie CLI 0.36.0 (August 21) adds configurable reasoning effort and improves session replay, daemon startup checks, and file synchronization.

options.name: Muse Code
options.notes: Meta's terminal coding agent with background subagents, persistent session history, and planning tools. Muse Spark 1.3 with max reasoning became available September 2, and Muse Voice Transcribe powers voice dictation from September 1.

options.name: Databricks Genie Code
options.notes: Databricks assistant for code, analysis, and workspace tasks. Scheduled tasks became generally available September 1, running recurring prompts as full sessions with results that users can continue in chat.
